Recursion

A function that solves a problem by asking a smaller copy of itself for help. Learn base cases, watch the call stack grow and unwind, tame repeated work with memoization, crack the Tower of Hanoi, walk nested data and trees, and turn deep recursion into loops.

Part 1

🪆Recursion: a function that calls itself

Open a Russian doll and you find a smaller doll that looks the same. Open that one and there is a smaller one again, until you reach a tiny solid doll that does not open. Recursion solves a problem the same way: it hands a smaller copy of the same problem to itself, until the problem is so small that the answer is obvious.

🛑 Base case

The tiny solid doll. A case simple enough to answer directly, such as factorial(1) = 1. Without it the function calls itself forever.

🔁 Recursive case

Shrink the problem and trust the smaller call: factorial(n) = n × factorial(n − 1). Every call must move closer to the base case.

Two questions for every recursive function: what is the smallest case I can answer straight away, and how do I make the problem one step smaller?
Part 2

📚The call stack: who is waiting for whom

When a function calls another, the computer puts a note on a pile called the call stack. The note, a stack frame, holds the local variables and the place to come back to. The newest call sits on top. When it returns, its frame is popped and the call below carries on from where it paused. That is exactly the last in, first out stack from the previous chapter.

LanguageToo deep givesTypical limit
PythonRecursionError1000 frames by default, sys.setrecursionlimit raises it
JavaStackOverflowErrordepends on the thread stack size, often around 10,000 frames
JavaScriptRangeError: Maximum call stack size exceededroughly 10,000 frames in Node and browsers
Recursion uses O(depth) memory for the frames, even when the function itself stores nothing. A recursion that goes n levels deep costs O(n) space.
Part 3

🌳Recursion trees and repeated work

When a function calls itself more than once, the calls branch like a family tree. Fibonacci calls itself twice, so fib(5) calls fib(4) and fib(3), and fib(4) calls fib(3) again. The same small problems are solved over and over, and the tree has about 2n nodes.

🧠 Memoization

Keep a map from input to answer. Before working, look it up. Each distinct input is then solved once, and fib(12) drops from 465 calls to 23.

📏 Reading the tree

Total work is the number of nodes times the work per node. The depth of the tree is the stack space. The Run time analysis chapter uses the same tree to solve recurrences.

Part 4

🙏Thinking recursively: the leap of faith

Do not try to follow every call in your head. Instead, assume the smaller call already works and ask only how to use its answer. To reverse "hello", trust that reverse("ello") gives "olle", then add "h" at the end. That trust is called the recursive leap of faith.

ProblemSmaller problemHow to use its answer
Reverse sreverse of s without its first letteradd the first letter at the end
Is s a palindromeis the middle (without both ends) a palindromealso check the two ends are equal
x to the power nx to the power n // 2square it, times x if n is odd
Fast power makes one call on half the exponent, so its recursion has only about log₂ n levels: 230 needs 30 calls, not a billion multiplications.
Part 5

🗼The Tower of Hanoi

Three pegs and a pile of discs, biggest at the bottom. Move the whole pile to another peg, one disc at a time, never putting a bigger disc on a smaller one. It looks hard, but recursion makes it three lines: move the top n − 1 discs out of the way, move the biggest disc, then move the n − 1 discs back on top of it.

The number of moves follows M(n) = 2 · M(n − 1) + 1, which gives M(n) = 2ⁿ − 1. A legend tells of monks moving 64 golden discs: at one move per second that is about 585 billion years.

Part 6

🧩Recursion on nested data and trees

Some data is recursive by nature. A folder holds files and other folders. A JSON document holds lists that hold objects that hold lists. A tree node has children that are trees themselves. For such data, recursion is not a trick but the most natural way to write the code.

📁 Folder sizes

The size of a folder is the size of its files plus the size of each subfolder, computed the same way. This is how disk usage tools work.

🌲 Trees

Height, size, sum and search in a tree are all "do it for the left, do it for the right, combine". The Trees chapter is full of them.

Part 7

🔄Tail calls and turning recursion into loops

A tail call is a recursive call that is the very last thing a function does, like return gcd(b, a % b). Nothing waits for its answer, so in principle its frame could be reused. Some languages (Scheme, Scala with @tailrec, Safari's JavaScript engine) do that. Python, Java and Node.js do not, so deep recursion still overflows.

WhenDo this
The recursion is a tail callrewrite it as a while loop that updates the arguments
It branches, like a tree walkkeep your own stack (a list) of work still to do
It repeats sub problemsmemoize, or build a table from the bottom up (dynamic programming)
Recursion is a way of thinking. Write the clear recursive version first, then change it to a loop only if the depth could be large.
